questions.text: अपने विस्तारित रूप में क्रोमेटीन 'डोरी पर बीड्स' के सदृश दिखाई पड़ते हैं। 'डोरी पर बीड्स' में 'डोरी' निरूपित करते हैं :
questions.text_english: In its extended 'beads-on-string' form of chromatin, the 'string' in the 'beads-on-string' represent :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Linker DNA. In the 'beads-on-string' model of chromatin, the 'beads' represent the nucleosomes (DNA wrapped around histone octamers), while the 'string' connecting the beads represents the Linker DNA. NHC proteins are non-histone chromosomal proteins involved in chromatin structure but do not form the string. Histones form the core of the nucleosome bead, not the string.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) लिंकर डीएनए है। 'डोरी पर बीड्स' मॉडल में, 'बीड्स' न्यूक्लियोसोम को दर्शाते हैं जबकि उन्हें जोड़ने वाली 'डोरी' लिंकर डीएनए होती है।

questions.text:
स्त्रियों (मानव मादा) में अंडजनन (ऊजेनेसिस) प्रक्रम के संदर्भ में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं :
(i) प्राथमिक अंडक के असमान विभाजन से एक वृहद द्वितीयक अंडक तथा एक लघु प्रथम ध्रुवीय पिंड की रचना होती है।
(ii) भ्रूणीय परिवर्धन के दौरान प्रत्येक भ्रूणीय अंडाशय के अंदर कुछ हजार अंडजननी (ऊगोनिया) विनिर्मित होती हैं।
(iii) प्राथमिक अंडक में अर्धसूत्री विभाजन-I प्रारंभ तो होता है परन्तु भ्रूण विकास की अवधि में यह अस्थाई रूप से पूर्वावस्था-I (प्रोफेज़-I) में ही अवरुद्ध हो जाता है।
(iv) निषेचन द्वितीयक अंडक के अर्धसूत्री विभाजन को पूर्ण होने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।
(v) प्राथमिक अंडक के अर्धसूत्री विभाजन द्वारा एक अंडाणु तथा एक ध्रुवीय पिंड का विनिर्माण होता है।
दिए गए विकल्पों से उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसके सभी कथन सत्य हैं :
questions.text_english:
Given below are few statements with reference to oogenesis in a human female :
(i) An unequal division of the primary oocyte forms a large secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.
(ii) A couple of thousands of oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary during embryonic development.
(iii) Primary oocytes start meiosis-I but it gets arrested temporarily at prophase-I during fetal development.
(iv) Fertilisation induces the completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte.
(v) A primary oocyte on meiosis forms an ovum and a polar body.
Choose the option with all true statements from the given options :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) (i), (iii), (iv). Statement (i) is true — the primary oocyte divides unequally to form a large secondary oocyte and a small first polar body. Statement (iii) is true — the primary oocyte begins meiosis-I but gets temporarily arrested at prophase-I during fetal development. Statement (iv) is true — fertilisation triggers completion of meiosis-II in the secondary oocyte. Statement (ii) is false because millions (not thousands) of oogonia are formed. Statement (v) is false because a primary oocyte on completing meiosis forms a secondary oocyte and a polar body, not directly an ovum.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) (i), (iii), (iv) है। कथन (i), (iii) और (iv) सत्य हैं। कथन (ii) असत्य है क्योंकि हजारों नहीं बल्कि लाखों ऊगोनिया बनती हैं। कथन (v) असत्य है क्योंकि प्राथमिक अंडक से सीधे अंडाणु नहीं बनता।

questions.text: थैलेसीमिया तथा दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता (सिकल सेल एनीमिया) दोनों ही ग्लोबिन अणु के संश्लेषण में उत्पन्न समस्या के कारण होते हैं। सही कथन का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Anaemia are both caused due to problem in globin molecule synthesis. Select the correct statement :

options.A: दोनों ही ग्लोबिन शृंखला के संश्लेषण में मात्रात्मक विकृति के कारण होते हैं।
options.B: थैलेसीमिया ग्लोबिन अणुओं की कम मात्रा में संश्लेषण होने के कारण होता है।
options.C: दात्र कोशिका अरक्तता ग्लोबिन अणुओं की मात्रात्मक समस्या के कारण होता है।
options.D: दोनों ही ग्लोबिन शृंखला के संश्लेषण में गुणात्मक विकृति के कारण होते हैं।

options_english.A: Both are due to a quantitative defect in globin chain synthesis.
options_english.B: Thalassemia is due to less synthesis of globin molecules.
options_english.C: Sickle cell anaemia is due to a quantitative problem of globin molecules.
options_english.D: Both are due to qualitative defect in globin chain synthesis.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Thalassemia is due to less synthesis of globin molecules. Thalassemia is a quantitative disorder where reduced amounts of globin chains are produced, leading to anaemia. Sickle cell anaemia, on the other hand, is a qualitative disorder caused by a point mutation (GAG to GUG) resulting in substitution of glutamic acid by valine, producing an abnormal haemoglobin-S. Option A is incorrect because they differ in type of defect. Option C is wrong because sickle cell anaemia is a qualitative, not quantitative, defect. Option D is wrong because thalassemia is quantitative.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। थैलेसीमिया एक मात्रात्मक विकार है जबकि सिकल सेल एनीमिया एक गुणात्मक विकार है।
questions.topic: Genetic Disorders — Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Anaemia

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए वंशावली चार्ट में एक अलिंगसूत्री प्रभावी विकार की वंशागति को दर्शाया गया है। प्रथम पीढ़ी का आनुवंशिक संयोजन (संरचना) है :
questions.text_english: A pedigree chart is shown below for a disease that is autosomal dominant. The genetic make-up of the first generation is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Aa, aa. In the pedigree, the disease is autosomal dominant. The Generation I female is affected and the male is unaffected (genotype aa). Since affected offspring and unaffected offspring appear in Generation II, the affected female must be heterozygous (Aa). If she were homozygous dominant (AA), all offspring would be affected. Since Generation II has unaffected individuals, the Generation I female must be Aa and the male must be aa. Hence, the first generation genotypes are Aa (female) and aa (male).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) Aa, aa है। प्रथम पीढ़ी में प्रभावित मादा विषमयुग्मजी (Aa) है और अप्रभावित नर समयुग्मजी अप्रभावी (aa) है।

questions.text: मानव में एलर्जी मास्ट कोशिकाओं द्वारा निम्नलिखित रसायनों के मोचन (निर्मुक्त) का परिणाम है :
questions.text_english: Allergy in humans is a result of release of the following chemicals from the mast cells :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Histamine and Serotonin. During an allergic reaction, IgE antibodies bind to mast cells. When the allergen re-enters the body, it cross-links the IgE antibodies on mast cells, triggering degranulation and release of histamine and serotonin. These chemicals cause typical allergy symptoms such as sneezing, watery eyes, and inflammation. Adrenaline, dopamine, endorphins, and GABA are not released by mast cells during allergic responses.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) हिस्टैमिन एवं सीरोटोनिन है। एलर्जिक प्रतिक्रिया में मास्ट कोशिकाओं से हिस्टैमिन और सीरोटोनिन मुक्त होते हैं।

questions.text:
उन कथनों को चुनिए जो पुष्पी पादपों में बहिःप्रजनन युक्तियों के लिए सत्य हैं।
(i) यह पर-परागण को हतोत्साहित करती हैं तथा स्वपरागण को सुनिश्चित करती हैं।
(ii) यह लाभकारी हैं क्योंकि इनसे अंतःप्रजनन अवनमन होता है।
(iii) स्व-अनिषेच्यता (असंगतता) अपने पुष्प के परागकणों द्वारा उसी पुष्प के बीजाण्ड के निषेचन को अवरोधित कर देता है।
(iv) स्वपरागण को रोकने (हतोत्साहित करने) के लिए कुछ प्रजातियों में पराग अवमुक्ति एवं वर्तिकाग्र ग्राह्यता समकालिक नहीं होतीं।
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Select the statements that are true for outbreeding devices in the flowering plants.
(i) They discourage cross-pollination and ensure self-pollination.
(ii) They are advantageous as they lead to inbreeding depression.
(iii) Self-incompatibility prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules.
(iv) To prevent self-pollination in some species pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised.
Choose the correct answer :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (iii) and (iv). Outbreeding devices in flowering plants promote cross-pollination, not self-pollination, so statement (i) is false. They reduce inbreeding depression by encouraging outbreeding, so statement (ii) is false. Statement (iii) is correct — self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising ovules of the same flower. Statement (iv) is also correct — asynchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity (dichogamy) is a common outbreeding device that prevents self-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) (iii) और (iv) है। बहिःप्रजनन युक्तियाँ पर-परागण को प्रोत्साहित करती हैं। कथन (iii) और (iv) सत्य हैं।

questions.text: माना जाता है कि मानव विकास के दौरान विकसित होने वाला प्रथम मानव-सदृश (जैसा) प्राणी था :
questions.text_english: The first human-like hominid evolved during human evolution is supposed to be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Homo habilis. Homo habilis, meaning 'handy man', is considered the first human-like hominid, appearing around 2 million years ago. They had a brain capacity of 650–800 cc and are believed to have used stone tools. Homo erectus evolved later and had a larger brain. Neanderthal man and Homo sapiens are more recent in evolutionary timeline.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) होमो हैबिलिस है। यह पहला मानव-सदृश होमिनिड माना जाता है जो लगभग 2 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व विकसित हुआ था।

questions.text: यदि अनुलेखित किए जाने वाले संरचनात्मक जीन की कोडिंग रज्जुक का न्यूक्लियोटाइड अनुक्रम 'TCC' (टीसीसी) है, तो स्थानांतरण प्रक्रिया के दौरान टीआरएनए (tRNA) के 3' सिरे पर जुड़े हुए ऐमीनो अम्ल को दी गई सूचना का उपयोग करके चुनिए।
questions.text_english: Use the given information to select the amino acid attached to the 3' end of tRNA during the process of translation, if the coding strand of the structural gene being transcribed has the nucleotide sequence 'TCC'.
questions.instruction_line: ऐमीनो अम्लों के लिए कोडॉन: AGG – आर्जिनीन, AAG – लाइसीन, UCC – सीरीन, GGA – ग्लाइसीन
questions.instruction_line_english: Codons for amino acids: AGG – Arginine, AAG – Lysine, UCC – Serine, GGA – Glycine
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Serine. The coding strand sequence is 5'-TCC-3'. During transcription, the template (non-coding) strand reads 3'-AGG-5', producing mRNA with the codon 5'-UCC-3'. The codon UCC codes for Serine as given in the table. The tRNA anticodon will be AGG, and Serine will be attached at its 3' end. Options A, B, and D are incorrect because AGG, AAG, and GGA are different codons not produced from the coding strand TCC.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) सीरीन है। कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड TCC से mRNA कोडॉन UCC बनता है जो सीरीन को कोड करता है।

questions.text: मानव के लिए परीक्षण पूर्व किसी टीके के सुरक्षा परीक्षण हेतु सर्वाधिक उपयोग किया जाने वाला पारजीवी जंतु (ट्रांसजेनिक एनिमल) है :
questions.text_english: The most widely used transgenic animal for testing the safety of vaccine before they are used in humans is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Mice. Transgenic mice are the most widely used transgenic animals in biomedical research, including vaccine safety testing before human use. They are ideal models due to their small size, short generation time, and well-characterized genetics. Transgenic mice have been engineered to carry human immune system genes, making them highly suitable for testing vaccine efficacy and safety. Rabbits, pigs, and sheep are used in research but not as commonly as mice for pre-clinical vaccine testing.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) चूहा है। ट्रांसजेनिक चूहों का उपयोग मानव पर टीके के प्रयोग से पूर्व सुरक्षा परीक्षण के लिए सर्वाधिक किया जाता है।

questions.text: यह सिद्ध करने के लिए कि डीएनए अर्धसंरक्षी प्रतिकृतियन करता है, मैथ्यू मेसेल्सन एवं फ्रैंकलिन स्टाल द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग में अपकेन्द्रण द्वारा 40 मिनट बाद संवर्धन से निष्कर्षित किए गए डीएनए को ठीक (सही) प्रकार से प्रदर्शित करने वाला आरेख है :
questions.text_english: The correct depiction of the experiment performed by Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl to prove that DNA replicates semi-conservatively on separation of DNA by centrifugation after 40 minutes is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). In the Meselson-Stahl experiment, bacteria were first grown in heavy ¹⁵N medium, then transferred to ¹⁴N medium. After 40 minutes (one generation/one replication), all DNA molecules should be hybrid — each consisting of one old ¹⁵N strand and one new ¹⁴N strand. On centrifugation, hybrid DNA (¹⁵N-¹⁴N) forms a single band at an intermediate position — neither at the heavy nor the light position. Option B correctly shows one band at an intermediate density, confirming semi-conservative replication.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। 40 मिनट बाद (एक पीढ़ी) सभी DNA अणु हाइब्रिड (¹⁵N-¹⁴N) होंगे जो मध्यवर्ती स्थिति पर एक ही बैंड बनाएंगे।

questions.text: मानव कल्याण के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले जैवसक्रिय अणु स्टैटिन का स्रोत है :
questions.text_english: Bioactive molecule statins used for human welfare are derived from :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Monascus purpureus. Statins are blood cholesterol-lowering agents (bioactive molecules) produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus. They competitively inhibit the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase, which is involved in cholesterol biosynthesis. Trichoderma polysporum produces cyclosporin A (an immunosuppressant). Propionibacterium shermanii is involved in vitamin B12 production. Aspergillus niger is used for citric acid production.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) मोनॉस्कस परप्यूरीअस है। यह यीस्ट स्टैटिन उत्पन्न करती है जो कोलेस्ट्रॉल कम करने वाला जैवसक्रिय अणु है।

questions.text: मटर के एक पौधे (पाइसम सैटाइवम) में फली का हरा रंग, फली के पीले रंग वाली फली पर प्रभावी है। एक क्रॉस जिसमें दोनों जनक में विषमयुग्मजी फली का हरा रंग है, की अगली प्रथम पीढ़ी संतति का दृश्यप्ररूप (फीनोटाइप) का अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: In a pea plant (Pisum sativum) green pod colour is dominant over yellow pod colour. The expected ratio of phenotypes of the first generation offspring in a cross between both the parents with heterozygous green pod colour will be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 3 : 1. When both parents are heterozygous (Gg × Gg), the cross produces offspring in the genotypic ratio 1 GG : 2 Gg : 1 gg. Since green (G) is dominant over yellow (g), both GG and Gg plants will show green pod colour while only gg plants will show yellow pod colour. Therefore, the phenotypic ratio is 3 green : 1 yellow, which is 3:1.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 3 : 1 है। Gg × Gg क्रॉस से 3 हरी (GG + Gg) : 1 पीली (gg) का अनुपात प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : मानव में ABO रक्त समूहन (रुधिर वर्ग) बहुअलील (मल्टीपल अलील) का उदाहरण है।
कारण (R) : मानव में ABO रुधिर समूहन समष्टि में दो से अधिक जीन एक ही लक्षण को नियंत्रित करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): ABO blood grouping in humans is an example of multiple allelism.
Reason (R): More than two genes in a population govern the same character in ABO blood grouping in humans.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct answer code for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion (A) is true — ABO blood grouping is indeed a classic example of multiple allelism where three alleles (Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i) exist for a single gene locus. However, the Reason (R) is false — multiple allelism does not mean more than two genes govern the trait; rather, it means more than two alleles exist for the same gene (locus) in the population, though any individual can carry only two of those alleles.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अभिकथन सत्य है क्योंकि ABO रक्त समूह बहुअलीलता का उदाहरण है, परन्तु कारण असत्य है — बहुअलीलता में दो से अधिक जीन नहीं बल्कि दो से अधिक अलील होते हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : संक्रमित पौधों से विषाणु-मुक्त (वायरस रहित) पौधे प्राप्त करने के लिए उनके विभज्योतकों का 'पात्रे' संवर्धन किया जाता है।

sub_questions.text_english: Justify the use of same Restriction Enzyme EcoR I to cut both the vector DNA and the alien DNA.

key_points: EcoR I cuts both DNAs at the same palindromic sequence, generating identical sticky ends
Compatible sticky ends allow the vector and alien DNA to join by complementary base pairing
This ensures successful ligation by DNA Ligase

sub_questions.solution: The same restriction enzyme EcoR I is used to cut both vector DNA and alien DNA because it generates identical sticky ends (5'-AATT-3' overhangs) on both fragments. These complementary sticky ends allow the vector DNA and the alien DNA to anneal (pair) with each other through hydrogen bonding. DNA Ligase then seals these ends covalently to form a stable recombinant DNA molecule. If different enzymes were used, incompatible ends would be produced and the two fragments could not join efficiently.

key_points: Enzyme A = DNA Ligase
Step-3 = Transformation
Same enzyme produces compatible sticky ends for ligation

questions.solution: (a) The enzyme A used in Step-1 is DNA Ligase, which joins the cut plasmid and alien DNA by sealing the phosphodiester bonds between their sticky ends. (b) Step-3 is called Transformation — the process of introducing recombinant DNA into a competent host bacterial cell (E. coli). (c) The same restriction enzyme EcoR I must be used for both DNAs because it generates identical complementary sticky ends (AATT overhangs) on both vector and alien DNA fragments. Only compatible sticky ends can anneal to each other and be subsequently joined by DNA Ligase to form the recombinant DNA molecule.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain how the interaction between sea anemone and clownfish is one of the best examples of commensalism in nature.
OR
(b) Correctly depict (also indicate the trophic level) and describe the ecological pyramid of biomass in sea with 40 standing crop of phytoplankton supporting 90 standing crop of zooplankton which further supports 120 small fishes.

key_points: (a) Clownfish benefits from protection among sea anemone tentacles; sea anemone is neither benefited nor harmed — classic commensalism
(b) Inverted pyramid: phytoplankton (T1, 40) → zooplankton (T2, 90) → small fish (T3, 120); biomass increases at higher trophic levels, forming an inverted pyramid

questions.solution:
(a) The interaction between sea anemone and clownfish is a classic example of commensalism, where one species benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed. The clownfish lives among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone, which provide it protection from predators. The clownfish benefits significantly — it gets shelter and safety. The sea anemone, however, is not visibly affected by the clownfish's presence; it neither gains nor loses from this association. Since only one species benefits and the other is unaffected, this relationship perfectly represents commensalism.

(b) In the sea, phytoplankton (Trophic Level 1, biomass = 40) supports zooplankton (Trophic Level 2, biomass = 90) which further supports small fishes (Trophic Level 3, biomass = 120). The food chain is: Phytoplankton (T1) → Zooplankton (T2) → Small Fishes (T3). Since biomass increases from lower to higher trophic levels (40 → 90 → 120), the ecological pyramid of biomass in the sea is an inverted pyramid, unlike terrestrial ecosystems where it is upright.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain how the immunity of a person is affected if there is atrophy (degeneration) of the thymus gland at an early stage of life.
OR
(b) (i) What are interferons? Explain their role in providing immunity to a person.
(ii) Which category of innate immunity defence barrier can interferons be classified into?

key_points: (a) Thymus produces T-lymphocytes; its early atrophy leads to severely compromised cell-mediated immunity (CMI) — person becomes immunodeficient
(b)(i) Interferons are proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect neighbouring uninfected cells from viral infection
(b)(ii) Physiological barrier (cytokine-based innate immunity)

questions.solution:
(a) The thymus gland is the primary lymphoid organ responsible for the maturation and differentiation of T-lymphocytes. If the thymus degenerates at an early stage of life, T-cells cannot mature properly. This severely compromises cell-mediated immunity (CMI). The person will be unable to mount effective immune responses against intracellular pathogens, viruses, and also tumour cells. The individual becomes highly susceptible to infections and may develop conditions similar to immunodeficiency diseases. Humoral immunity may be partially retained, but CMI will be severely deficient.

(b)(i) Interferons are glycoprotein molecules secreted by virus-infected cells. When a cell is infected by a virus, it releases interferons that signal neighbouring uninfected cells to produce antiviral proteins, thereby protecting them from viral infection. They do not directly destroy the virus but create an antiviral state in surrounding cells, thus limiting the spread of viral infection in the body.
(ii) Interferons can be classified under the physiological barriers of innate immunity, as they are chemical substances produced by the body as a non-specific defense mechanism.

UUA in Frame 1 is Leucine (not stop); UAA in Frame 2 would be a stop codon — Frame 2 specifies fewer amino acids

questions.solution:
For Frame 1 (5' CUCGCUUGCCGAUCAAGGGUUA 3'): There are 22 nucleotides total. Reading in triplets from the first nucleotide: CUC-GCU-UGC-CGA-UCA-AGG-GUU-A. This gives 7 complete codons with 1 nucleotide remaining. There is no UAA, UAG, or UGA stop codon in these 7 codons, so 7 amino acids are specified.

For Frame 2 (5' GUGGCACUCAGUCCUUAAUGGCG 3'): There are 23 nucleotides. Reading in triplets from the first nucleotide: GUG-GCA-CUC-AGU-CCU-UAA-UGG-CG. The sixth codon is UAA, which is a stop codon. Translation terminates at UAA, so only 5 amino acids are coded (the stop codon itself does not code for an amino acid). Therefore, Frame 1 specifies 7 amino acids and Frame 2 specifies 5 amino acids.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Write the function of each of the following:
(I) Seminal Plasma
(II) Acrosome of human sperm
(ii) Differentiate between menarche and menopause.
OR
(b) (i) How is apomixis different from parthenocarpy?
(ii) Why are apples and cashews not called true fruits?

key_points: (a)(i)(I) Seminal plasma nourishes and facilitates transport of sperms
(a)(i)(II) Acrosome contains hydrolytic enzymes (acrosin) that help penetrate the egg
(a)(ii) Menarche = onset of first menstruation at puberty; Menopause = cessation of menstruation around age 50
(b)(i) Apomixis = seed formation without fertilisation; Parthenocarpy = fruit development without fertilisation
(b)(ii) In apple and cashew, the thalamus/receptacle develops into fleshy part, not the ovary wall, so they are false/pseudo fruits

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(I) Seminal plasma is the fluid component of semen secreted by accessory reproductive glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral glands). It provides nutrition to the sperms, maintains their motility, neutralises the acidic environment of the female reproductive tract, and facilitates their transport towards the egg.
(a)(i)(II) The acrosome is a cap-like structure on the head of the sperm derived from the Golgi body. It contains hydrolytic enzymes, including acrosin and hyaluronidase, which help the sperm to penetrate the zona pellucida and plasma membrane of the egg during fertilisation.
(a)(ii) Menarche refers to the onset of the first menstrual cycle in a girl at puberty (around 13–14 years). Menopause refers to the permanent cessation of the menstrual cycle in a woman, usually around the age of 45–50 years.

(b)(i) Apomixis is the production of seeds without fertilisation (asexual seed formation), maintaining the genetic constitution of the mother plant. Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, resulting in seedless fruits.
(b)(ii) In a true fruit, the pericarp develops from the ovary wall. In apples, the fleshy edible part develops from the thalamus (receptacle), and the true fruit is the hard core inside. In cashews, the fleshy part is the swollen peduncle (accessory tissue), and the true fruit is the hard kidney-shaped structure. Since the edible part is not derived from the ovary, they are called false fruits or pseudo-fruits.

questions.text_english:
According to a recent wildlife report, the biggest threat to the tiger's survival in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) was found to be a small, beautiful flower, Lantana camara, a tropical American shrub, that invaded 40% of India's tiger range. Tamil Nadu department's Lantana weed eradication drive helped to restore the dying MTR thereby also reducing human-wildlife conflicts. MTR is home to 25 species of grasses and legumes.
(a) Explain how did the removal of Lantana help in restoring the dying Mudumalai Tiger Reserve.
(b) Why is the invasion of Lantana camara a cause of concern in MTR.

key_points: Lantana is an invasive alien species that displaces native grasses and legumes — primary food source for prey animals of tigers
Removal of Lantana allowed restoration of 25 native grass/legume species, restoring prey base, improving habitat for tigers
Lantana is a cause of concern because it is a fast-spreading invasive species threatening biodiversity and disrupting the food chain

questions.solution:
(a) Lantana camara is an invasive alien species from tropical America that rapidly spreads and displaces native vegetation. In MTR, it had taken over 40% of the area, eliminating native grasses and legumes that serve as food for herbivores like deer, bison, and other prey animals of tigers. With the decline of prey animals, tigers were starving and dying. When the Tamil Nadu department removed Lantana through their weed eradication drive, native grass and legume species (25 species) were restored. This improved the grazing ground for prey animals, replenishing their population, which in turn provided adequate food for tigers. The restored habitat also reduced human-wildlife conflicts as animals no longer strayed into human settlements in search of food.

(b) Lantana camara is a cause of concern in MTR because it is an aggressive invasive alien species that grows faster than native plants, outcompetes them for space, light, and nutrients, and reduces biodiversity. It threatens the 25 species of native grasses and legumes that form the ecological base of the food chain in MTR. Its spread disrupts the prey base of tigers, thereby endangering the entire tiger population of the reserve.

questions.text_english:
Gregor Mendel used true-breeding pea lines to conduct his hybridisation experiments in garden pea.
(a) Explain what is meant by true-breeding pea lines.
(b) State the three important points of law of dominance as proposed by Gregor Mendel.

key_points: True-breeding lines: plants that produce same character generation after generation after self-pollination — homozygous
Law of Dominance: (1) Characters exist in pairs; (2) In a heterozygote, one allele dominates the other; (3) The recessive allele is not lost and reappears in F2

questions.solution:
(a) True-breeding pea lines refer to plants that have been self-pollinating for many generations and always produce offspring with the same phenotype as the parent plant. These plants are homozygous for the trait in question, meaning both alleles for a given character are identical (e.g., TT for tallness or tt for dwarfness). True-breeding plants show stable inheritance with no segregation of characters, which is why Mendel used them as parental plants to ensure pure starting material for his experiments.

(b) The three important points of the Law of Dominance proposed by Mendel are: First, characters are controlled by discrete units called factors (genes), which always occur in pairs. Second, in an organism carrying two different alleles for a character (heterozygous), only one allele expresses itself phenotypically — this is the dominant allele — while the other allele remains unexpressed in the phenotype — this is the recessive allele. Third, when the organism is heterozygous, the recessive allele is not lost or destroyed; it remains in the organism and can reappear in the phenotype in subsequent generations when two recessive alleles come together.

questions.text_english: Enlist one advantage and two disadvantages of green revolution.

key_points: Advantage: Significant increase in food grain production leading to food security
Disadvantage 1: Excessive use of fertilisers and pesticides led to soil and water pollution
Disadvantage 2: Reduction in genetic diversity as only high-yielding varieties were cultivated, making crops vulnerable to new diseases

questions.solution:
One major advantage of the Green Revolution is that it led to a dramatic increase in the production of food grains, especially wheat and rice, in countries like India. The introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYV) of crops ensured food security for millions of people and helped nations become self-sufficient in food production.

Two important disadvantages of the Green Revolution are: First, the heavy reliance on chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and herbicides caused significant environmental damage, including soil degradation, water pollution, and harmful effects on non-target organisms and biodiversity. Second, the widespread cultivation of only a few high-yielding varieties led to a reduction in genetic diversity (genetic erosion) of crop plants. This monoculture made crops more vulnerable to new pests, diseases, and climatic stresses, as the genetic resistance present in traditional varieties was lost.

questions.text_english:
Given below is a flower with its characteristic features specialised for the most common type of abiotic pollination.
(a) Name the mode of abiotic pollination that will be adopted by the given plant species in the above picture.
(b) State the need of exposed large feathery stigmas for the flower.
(c) What will be the two important adaptations in the pollen grains of the flowers pollinated by the above mode of pollination?
(d) What could be the probable reason for the petals being small and non-green?

key_points: (a) Anemophily (wind pollination)
(b) Large feathery stigmas provide a larger surface area to trap airborne pollen grains
(c) Pollen grains: light and small; dry/non-sticky surface (or winged for some)
(d) Small, non-green petals do not attract insects — energy saved as wind pollination requires no insect attraction

questions.solution:
(a) The mode of abiotic pollination adopted by this plant is Anemophily (wind pollination). The features visible in the diagram — versatile anthers, large feathery stigmas, and small non-green petals — are all characteristic adaptations for wind pollination.

(b) The large, feathery (branched) stigmas are exposed outside the flower to provide a maximum surface area for trapping pollen grains carried by wind. Since wind pollination is non-directional and pollen dispersal is random, having a larger catching surface greatly increases the probability of pollen grains landing on the stigma.

(c) Pollen grains adapted for wind pollination are: (i) light in weight and very small in size so that they can be easily carried by wind over long distances, and (ii) produced in enormous quantities to compensate for the wastage due to random dispersal, and their surface is dry and non-sticky (unlike insect-pollinated pollen) to prevent clumping.

(d) The petals in wind-pollinated flowers are small and non-green because they do not need to attract any animal pollinator. Wind-pollinated plants save energy by not investing in producing large, colourful, or scented petals. The reduction in petal size also prevents them from obstructing the free movement of pollen and the accessibility of stigma to airborne pollen.

questions.text_english: Explain the process of formation of placenta in a human female after the implantation of the blastocyst in the endometrium of the uterus.

key_points: Blastocyst implants in endometrium; trophoblast differentiates into cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast
Chorionic villi develop from trophoblast and interdigitate with uterine tissue
Placenta is formed — structural and functional unit connecting fetus to mother for exchange of nutrients, gases, and wastes

questions.solution: After implantation of the blastocyst in the endometrium, the outer layer of the blastocyst called the trophoblast differentiates into two layers: the inner cytotrophoblast and the outer syncytiotrophoblast. The syncytiotrophoblast cells actively invade and erode the endometrial tissue. The trophoblast cells proliferate and form finger-like projections called chorionic villi that grow into the endometrial tissue. Simultaneously, the uterine endometrial cells also proliferate and surround these chorionic villi, forming interdigitating maternal and foetal tissues. This complex structure of chorionic villi embedded in maternal uterine tissue forms the placenta. The placenta is a special temporary organ that serves as a structural and functional link between the developing embryo (foetus) and the mother. It facilitates the exchange of nutrients, oxygen, and waste products between the foetal and maternal blood, although the two circulations do not mix directly.

questions.text_english: Explain the biological treatment of primary effluent when passed into the large aeration tanks in a sewage treatment plant (STP).

key_points: Primary effluent passed to large aeration tanks — this is secondary treatment
Aerobic microbes (bacteria) digest/break down organic matter and form flocs (masses of bacteria + fungal filaments)
BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is reduced; flocs settle as activated sludge; effluent becomes cleaner

questions.solution: When primary effluent (sewage from which large solids have been removed by sedimentation) is passed into large aeration tanks in a Sewage Treatment Plant, secondary biological treatment takes place. In these tanks, the effluent is vigorously agitated and air is pumped in to maintain aerobic conditions. Aerobic heterotrophic microorganisms, mainly bacteria, grow rapidly in the tank and consume the organic matter present in the sewage as their food. These bacteria form mesh-like masses called flocs, which are aggregates of bacteria held together by fungal filaments in a slime matrix. As the bacteria break down the organic matter, the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of the effluent decreases significantly. BOD is a measure of the organic matter or pollutant load in the water. When most of the BOD is consumed, the flocs settle at the bottom of a settling tank to form activated sludge, while the clear supernatant effluent can be safely discharged or passed for tertiary treatment.

sub_questions.solution: Both (i) Humans and Macaque and (ii) Humans and Frog represent Divergent evolution. sub_questions.text_english: What do the biochemical similarities in haemoglobin suggest about the evolutionary relationship between humans, frog and lamprey?

sub_questions.solution: The biochemical similarities in haemoglobin among humans, frog, and lamprey suggest that all three share a common ancestor from whom haemoglobin was inherited. The fact that all three organisms possess haemoglobin as their oxygen-carrying molecule indicates a common evolutionary origin. However, the degree of similarity differs — humans and frogs share 67 amino acid differences, while humans and lamprey share 125 differences, indicating that frogs are more closely related to humans than lampreys are. sub_questions.solution:

This is because the haemoglobin of macaque differs from human haemoglobin in only 8 amino acids, while lamprey haemoglobin differs from human haemoglobin in 125 amino acids. Fewer amino acid differences indicate that macaques and humans share a more recent common ancestor and have diverged less from each other during evolution. Since haemoglobin is a slowly evolving conserved protein, the degree of molecular similarity is a reliable indicator of evolutionary closeness.

(ii) Dog is more closely related to humans than frog in evolutionary terms. The haemoglobin of dogs differs from that of humans by 32 amino acids, whereas frog haemoglobin differs by 67 amino acids. This significantly smaller difference in amino acid sequence indicates that dogs share a more recent common ancestor with humans and have undergone less evolutionary divergence compared to frogs.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Give the full form of 'ELISA'. Write the principle on which ELISA test is based.
(ii) Describe all the methods used to treat or cure Adenosine deaminase deficiency in humans.
OR
(b) Explain the process of separation and isolation of DNA fragments by a typical gel electrophoresis.

key_points: (a)(i) ELISA = Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay; principle: antigen-antibody interaction detected by enzyme-linked antibody producing colour change
(a)(ii) ADA deficiency: enzyme replacement therapy; bone marrow transplantation; gene therapy (lymphocytes treated with functional ADA gene)

(b) DNA gel electrophoresis: DNA loaded on agarose gel, current applied — negatively charged DNA migrates to positive electrode, smaller fragments move faster, stained with ethidium bromide, visualised under UV, cut and isolated

questions.solution:
(a)(i) ELISA stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. The principle of ELISA is based on the highly specific antigen-antibody interaction. In this test, the antigen (if present in the sample) binds to a specific antibody that is conjugated (linked) to an enzyme. When the enzyme's substrate is added, it reacts with the enzyme to produce a coloured product. The presence and intensity of this colour indicate the presence and amount of antigen in the sample. ELISA can be used to detect antigens (such as HIV proteins) or specific antibodies (such as anti-HIV antibodies) in a patient's serum, making it a widely used diagnostic tool.

(a)(ii) Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency is a genetic disorder where the ADA enzyme is non-functional, leading to accumulation of toxic metabolites that destroy T-lymphocytes, causing severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). The methods used to treat or cure ADA deficiency are: First, enzyme replacement therapy — functional ADA enzyme can be periodically injected into the patient; this is not a permanent cure. Second, bone marrow transplantation — transplanting healthy bone marrow cells that can produce functional T-cells; this can be a cure if a compatible donor is found. Third, gene therapy — lymphocytes are isolated from the patient's blood, the functional ADA gene (cDNA) is introduced into these lymphocytes in vitro using a retroviral vector, and the genetically corrected lymphocytes are infused back into the patient. This is the first successful gene therapy attempted in humans for ADA deficiency, though repeated infusions are needed.

(b) Gel electrophoresis is the technique used to separate DNA fragments based on their size. The procedure involves the following steps: First, an agarose gel is prepared and placed in an electrophoresis chamber filled with buffer. The agarose gel acts as a molecular sieve. Second, the DNA sample mixed with a loading dye is loaded into the wells of the gel. A DNA ladder (marker with known fragment sizes) is also loaded in a separate well for comparison. Third, an electric current is applied across the gel. Since DNA is negatively charged (due to phosphate groups), it migrates towards the positive electrode (anode). The gel matrix resists the movement of larger fragments more than smaller ones, causing size-based separation — smaller fragments move faster and travel further, while larger fragments move more slowly and remain closer to the wells. Fourth, after electrophoresis, the gel is stained with ethidium bromide (EtBr), an intercalating dye. When the stained gel is exposed to UV light, the DNA bands appear as bright orange bands. Fifth, specific bands can be excised (cut) from the gel, and the DNA can be isolated from the gel piece using elution. This isolated DNA can then be used for downstream applications such as cloning or sequencing.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Describe the population growth curve applicable in a population of any species in nature that has limited resources at its disposal.
(ii) Give the equation of this growth curve.
(iii) Name the growth curve and depict a graphical plot for this type of population growth.
OR
(b) (i) Explain the Species-Area relationship within a natural forest and also predict the nature of graph when species richness is plotted against the area for a wide variety of taxa.
(ii) Depict the graphical relationship between species richness and area.
(iii) Give the equation of the Species-Area relationship for a wide variety of taxa on a logarithmic scale.

key_points: (a)(i) Logistic growth / S-shaped (sigmoid) curve when resources are limited
(a)(ii) dN/dt = rN(K-N/K), where K = carrying capacity
(a)(iii) Logistic growth curve — S-shaped; population rises slowly, then rapidly, then levels off at K
(b)(i) More species in larger areas; graph is a rectangular hyperbola for small areas; linear on log scale
(b)(ii) Species richness vs area: rectangular hyperbola or straight line on log-log scale
(b)(iii) log S = log C + Z log A

questions.solution:
(a)(i) When a population has limited resources at its disposal, it does not grow indefinitely. Initially, when population size is small and resources are abundant, the population grows slowly (lag phase). Then it grows rapidly (log phase). However, as the population increases, resources become scarce, intraspecific competition intensifies, and environmental resistance increases (due to food shortage, disease, predation, and waste accumulation). This causes the growth rate to slow down progressively until the population size stabilises at the maximum number that the environment can sustain, called the Carrying Capacity (K). This type of growth, when plotted against time, produces an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve known as the logistic growth curve.

(a)(ii) The equation for logistic growth is: dN/dt = rN [(K − N) / K], where dN/dt is the rate of change of population size, r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase, N is the current population size, and K is the carrying capacity of the environment. When N is much less than K, the term in brackets approaches 1 and growth is approximately exponential. When N approaches K, the term approaches 0 and growth ceases.

(a)(iii) This type of growth is called the Logistic Growth Curve or the S-shaped (sigmoid) curve. [A graphical plot should show: x-axis = Time, y-axis = Population size (N); curve starts low, rises in an S-shape, and flattens at K (carrying capacity). The inflection point is at N = K/2.]

(b)(i) In a natural forest, larger areas contain more species than smaller areas — this is the Species-Area relationship. When a scientist explores a larger geographic area, they encounter more habitats, more microhabitats, and more ecological niches, supporting a greater diversity of species. When species richness is plotted against area on a normal scale, a rectangular hyperbola is obtained. When the same relationship is plotted on a logarithmic scale (log-log plot), a straight line with a positive slope is obtained.

(b)(ii) [A graph should be drawn with species richness (S) on y-axis and Area (A) on x-axis, showing a rectangular hyperbola. On a log-log plot, the same relationship gives a straight line.]

(b)(iii) The equation for the Species-Area relationship on a logarithmic scale for a wide variety of taxa is: log S = log C + Z log A, where S is the species richness, A is the area, Z is the slope of the line (regression coefficient, typically between 0.1 and 0.2 for small areas, and around 0.6 for large continents), and C is the Y-intercept (related to species richness in a unit area).

(ii) इन पौधों में द्विनिषेचन के पश्चात् निर्मित उत्पादों (संरचनाओं) का भावी परिणाम लिखिए।
अथवा
(ख) (i) पुरुषों (मानव नर जनन तंत्र) में वृषण पालिका (टेस्टिकुलर लोब्युल्स) की संरचना की व्याख्या कीजिए। शुक्रजनक नलिकाओं में पाई जाने वाली दो प्रकार की कोशिकाओं के नाम लिखिए तथा उनकी भूमिका बताइए।
(ii) शुक्रजनन के प्रक्रम में अधश्चेतक (हाइपोथैलेमिक) हॉर्मोन (GnRH) की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Explain how does double fertilisation take place in a flowering plant.
(ii) Write the fate of the products of double fertilization in these plants.
OR
(b) (i) Explain the structure of testicular lobules in human male reproductive system. Name the two types of cells present in the seminiferous tubules and state their role.
(ii) Describe the role of hypothalamic hormone GnRH in spermatogenesis.

key_points: (a)(i) Pollen tube reaches embryo sac; one male gamete fuses with egg (syngamy) → zygote; second male gamete fuses with secondary nucleus (triple fusion) → primary endosperm nucleus; these two fusion events together = double fertilisation
(a)(ii) Zygote → embryo; primary endosperm nucleus → endosperm (nutritive tissue); ovule → seed; ovary → fruit
(b)(i) Testicular lobules contain 1–3 seminiferous tubules; two cell types: Spermatogonia (sperm-producing) and Sertoli cells (nutritive/supportive); Leydig cells present in interstitial tissue

(b)(ii) GnRH from hypothalamus stimulates anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH; FSH acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate spermatogenesis; LH acts on Leydig cells to produce testosterone which regulates spermatogenesis

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Double fertilisation is a unique feature of angiosperms (flowering plants). After pollination, the pollen grain germinates on the stigma and produces a pollen tube that grows through the style and enters the ovule through the micropyle. The pollen tube carries two male gametes (non-motile). Inside the embryo sac (female gametophyte), the following two fusions occur simultaneously: First, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell (female gamete) in a process called syngamy or true fertilisation, producing a diploid zygote (2n). Second, the other male gamete fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (formed by fusion of two polar nuclei), in a process called triple fusion, producing the triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Since two fusions take place in the embryo sac, the phenomenon is called double fertilisation, first described by Nawaschin in 1898.

(a)(ii) The fate of the products of double fertilisation: The zygote (2n) undergoes mitotic divisions to develop into the embryo, which is the future plant. The primary endosperm nucleus (3n) divides mitotically to form the endosperm — a nutritive tissue that provides food to the developing embryo. The ovule develops into the seed (containing embryo and endosperm surrounded by seed coat derived from integuments). The ovary develops into the fruit (pericarp derived from ovary wall). Other floral parts like petals, sepals, and stamens generally wither and fall off.

(b)(i) Each testis is divided into about 250 compartments called testicular lobules. Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules, which are the sites of sperm production. The seminiferous tubules are lined with two types of cells: Spermatogonia (also called male germ cells or sperm mother cells), which are the cells that undergo meiosis and spermatogenesis to produce spermatids and ultimately spermatozoa (sperm). Sertoli cells (also called nurse cells), which are large supporting cells that provide nutrition to the developing spermatids, secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP), and maintain the blood-testis barrier. In the interstitial spaces between the seminiferous tubules are the Leydig cells (interstitial cells), which are not inside the tubules but synthesise and secrete androgens (mainly testosterone), which are essential for spermatogenesis and development of male secondary sexual characters.

(b)(ii) GnRH (Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone) is secreted by the hypothalamus. Its role in spermatogenesis is as follows: GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates it to secrete two gonadotropins — FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) and LH (Luteinizing Hormone). FSH acts on the Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules, stimulating them to secrete androgen-binding protein (ABP) and to support the process of spermatogenesis. LH acts on the Leydig cells (interstitial cells) located in the intertubular spaces and stimulates them to synthesise and secrete testosterone (androgens). Testosterone, in turn, is essential for the completion of spermatogenesis, including the maturation of spermatids into spermatozoa. Thus, GnRH indirectly regulates the entire process of spermatogenesis through a cascade of hormonal signals.
questions.solution_hindi:
(क)(i) द्विनिषेचन: एक नर युग्मक + अंडकोशिका → युग्मनज (2n); दूसरा नर युग्मक + द्वितीयक केंद्रक → प्राथमिक भ्रूणपोष केंद्रक (3n)।
(ii) युग्मनज → भ्रूण; PEN → भ्रूणपोष; बीजांड → बीज; अंडाशय → फल।
(ख)(i) वृषण पालिकाओं में शुक्रजनक नलिकाएँ हैं जिनमें शुक्राणुजन (शुक्राणु बनाने वाली) और सर्टोली कोशिकाएँ (पोषण देने वाली) होती हैं।
(ii) GnRH → अग्र पीयूष ग्रंथि → FSH + LH → सर्टोली कोशिकाएँ + लेडिग कोशिकाएँ → शुक्रजनन।
